newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ERICSSON SEES OPERATOR SERVICE UP - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: ERICSSON SEES OPERATOR SERVICE UP - REPORT.

text.p: Swedish telecoms group Ericsson sees services for telephone network operators as an important future growth area, business daily Finanstidningen reported on Wednesday.
"There is a large potential for Ericsson when it comes to services for operators," Ericsson chief executive Lars Ramqvist told the newspaper.
"It is still a small area for Ericsson but it is growing rapidly."
It is mainly the U.S. market for services, such as planning, construction, integration and operating the network, that is growing while the European market is more sluggish, the newspaper said.
Demand for services has increased as telephone networks have become more complicated and Ericsson expects operators to concentrate in the future more on marketing and less on technical issues.
"If we look a few years ahead, operator services may become a significant operation for Ericsson," Ramqvist was quoted as saying.
Currently, operator services only account for a few percent of Ericsson's sales.
At the business area Public Telecommunications, operator services amount to 10 percent of sales while they account for a much smaller portion of sales on the mobile side.

In the year 2000, operator services are expected to make up 15 percent of sales at Public Telecommunications and similar figures are expected on the mobile side shortly thereafter, Finanstidningen said.
Growth is then seen continuing but Ericsson does not expect it to reach 50 percent of sales, as it does for computer companies IBM and Digital, the newspaper said.
Ramqvist stressed that Ericsson will not compete with operators and that the company does not intend to buy operators.
